title_content.content: Gold(I)-Catalyzed [2 + 2] and [3 + 2] Cycloadditions of 1,1- Difluoroallenes with Aldehydes: Switchable Syntheses of Fluorinated Oxetanes and Furans

paragraph_content.content: Daisuke Miyazaki, Konami Kudo, Yusuke Fujiki, Natsumi Watanabe, Toru Matsui,* Junji Ichikawa,* and Kohei Fuchibe*

2] cycloadditions with aldehydes using Au(I) catalysts. An AuCl catalyst enabled an α,β-selective [2 + 2] cycloaddition of 1,1-difluoroallenes, yielding (E)-3-alkylidene-2,2-difluorooxetanes. Conversely, an AuCl(IPr)−AgSbF catalyst facilitated an α,γ-selective [3 + 2] cycloaddition, followed by dehydrofluorination to produce aromatized 2-fluorofurans. DFT calculations (B3LYP level) suggested that the former reaction proceeded through Au(III)- containing metallacycles, while the latter involved cyclic Au(I) carbenoids.

The reaction was more eficient in toluene (a 77% yield of 5a), exhibiting (i) regioselectivities in terms of both 1,1-difluoroallenes 3 and aldehydes 4 and (ii) diastereoselectivity in terms of the formation of the alkylidene moiety (entry 2). The

cycloaddition of 1,1-difluoroallenes 3a−c (Figure 3A) with 4a yielded (E)-3-alkylidene-2,2-difluorooxetanes 5a−c in 53%− 72% yields (Table 2). Aldehydes 4c−g, 4j, and 4k (Figure 3B) similarly reacted with 3a to produce the corresponding 2,2- difluorooxetanes 5d−j in 43%−84% yields (Table 2).<sup>19</sup> The four-membered cyclic structure and the geometry of the alkylidene moiety in the products were confirmed by singlecrystal X-ray structural analysis of 5e (CCDC 2141882).

Toste et al. investigated the reaction pathways for intramolecular
cycloadditions of fluorine-free allenes with dienes. They found that
cycloadducts were formed through the ring contraction of the common sevenmembered cyclic

carbenoid intermediates.<sup>23</sup> However, for the formation of 2,2-difluorooxetanes 5, the ring contraction mechanism appears unlikely owing to (A) the low activation energy for the β-hydrogen migration step (1.23 kcal/mol, TS2<sup>[3+2]</sup>, Scheme 2) and (B) the inherent ring strain of the forming four-membered oxetanes.<sup>24</sup>
cycloadditions of 1,1-difluoroallenes with aldehydes were successfully achieved. An AuCl catalyst yielded (E)-3- alkylidene-2,2-difluorooxetanes as

(19) The AuCl-catalyzed [2 + 2] cycloaddition of 3a with pmethoxybenzaldehyde and o-methoxybenzaldehyde (4i) resulted in a mixture of nonfluorinated unidentifiable materials. The [2 + 2] cycloaddition of 3a with i-PrCHO successfully aforded the corresponding 2,2-difluorooxetane, which rapidly decomposed upon isolation.

(20) The AuCl(IPr)−AgSbF -catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition of 3a with p-methoxybenzaldehyde aforded the corresponding product, albeit in a decreased yield (30%). The difluoroallene 3a also reacted with i-PrCHO but did not aford the corresponding product.

(21) Our theoretical calculations indicated that the bond orders of the two Au−C “bonds” involved in Int1<sup>[2+2]</sup> are close to each other [0.615 for Au−C(difluoroallene) and 0.646 for Au−C(aldehyde)]. We thus consider that the intermediate Int1<sup>[2+2]</sup> should be recognized as a cyclic Au(III) complex rather than an Au(I) species with electronic interaction between the gold atom and the carbocation.
